issues.description: Method return type mismatch for Stock.take(String): The problem statement UML (and the exercise description) declares Stock.take(String) as returning int (representing remaining quantity or -1 on failure). The solution implementation defines public int take(String ingredient) returning the new quantity or -1. The template implementation defines public boolean take(String ingredient) returning true/false. This inconsistency prevents students from implementing SealSaloon methods (e.g., checkOrderReady and calculateTotalPrice) that rely on an int return value (to detect -1 vs a non-negative remaining quantity) and will lead to compilation or logic errors if not reconciled.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the template's Stock.take(String) signature and implementation to return int (e.g., public int take(String ingredient)) and implement it to: return the new quantity after decrementing by one if the ingredient exists and quantity >= 1, otherwise return -1. Ensure any code that called the old boolean API is updated to handle int results. This will align the template with the UML/problem statement and the provided solution and allow SealSaloon implementations to compile and behave as intended.

issues.description: Concept: the Stock.take operation that removes one unit of an ingredient and reports the result. Problem statement / UML declares Stock.take(String) -> int (an integer status/remaining-quantity contract). Template repository implements public boolean take(String) (returns true/false). Solution repository implements public int take(String) (returns -1 when missing/out-of-stock and remaining quantity otherwise). This naming/signature mismatch (boolean vs int) means students cannot unambiguously map the required contract in the problem statement to the template API: the problem and solution expect numeric status (-1/remaining quantity) while the template exposes only a boolean, which changes how SealSaloon logic must be written (e.g., checks against -1 vs boolean checks). This inconsistency therefore creates confusion and blocks straightforward implementation of SealSaloon methods that rely on the int contract.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the template Stock.take method with the problem statement and solution: change the template signature to public int take(String ingredient) and implement the return convention used in the solution (return -1 if the ingredient is missing or out of stock, otherwise decrement quantity by one and return the remaining quantity). Update any template comments or example usages to reflect the int contract so students clearly see the intended behavior.
